body:
Overall, a pretty nice cleanup. Lots of stuff to love, and it should decrease the cognitive overload.

I'm not a fan of the short options. They save space in the code, yes, but at the cost of forcing a reader to either trust that you know what you're doing, or open up a manpage and search for each of the options (or to have encyclopedic knowledge of curl flags). I actually wouldn't object to all the options being made long-form, except that many commands don't have them (for example, AFAIK `unzip` is short-form only).

There's also a lot of dumb gotchas shell, so I've marked a whole bunch of the ones I saw. These range from "if you don't have a very core utility installed, the script errors out with a message" to  "this can silently fail while allowing the script to advance to the next stage." Feel free to reject or ask about these notes!

Once we've touched up the PR a little bit, I'll throw it through the wringer on MacOS/Windows.
